articles.title: Caleb Williams Injured, Latest on Bears Star's Timeline to Return After Being Carted Off vs. Vikings
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears' season may have just taken a very concerning turn.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears' season may have just taken a very concerning turn.

Franchise quarterback Caleb Williams appeared to suffer a serious leg injury during Sunday's 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings while scrambling from the pocket. He was later rul ed out with a hamstring injury.

Head coach Ben Johnson provided an update after the game:

Mike Florio of ProFootballTalk reported that the Bears are hopeful it will be diagnosed as a Grade 1 injury. However, the team will not know the severity until Williams undergoes an MRI on Monday.

Williams is heading into his third season with the Bears after leading his team to an NFC North title and the divisional round of the playoffs in 2025.

He completed 58.1 percent of his passes last season for 3,942 yards with 27 touchdowns and seven interceptions.

Williams also added 77 carries for 388 rushing yards and three touchdowns while leading the Bears to an 11-6 record.

Although he took significantly fewer sacks during his sophomore campaign, going from a historic 68 sacks as rookie to 24 sacks last season, Williams also saw his completion percentage drop.

Bears coach Ben Johnson made improving Williams' accuracy a focus during training camp this offseason.

Taking that step forward this fall will require a healthy Williams. If he is sidelined for any length of time, however, the Bears will turn to Case Keenum in the short term.

articles.title: Bryce Young, Shough and Top Fantasy Waiver-Wire QBs After Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels Injuries
articles.summary: Caleb Williams appeared to suffer major hamstring during Sunday's contest against the Minnesota Vikings, a huge concern for the Chicago Bears going forward.
articles.body:
Caleb Williams appeared to suffer major hamstring during Sunday's contest against the Minnesota Vikings, a huge concern for the Chicago Bears going forward.

Later in the day, Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels also had to be carted off against the Dallas Cowboys:

Fantasy enthusiasts who rostered Williams and Daniels may also need to start considering other options. Below we'll break down some of the players to have on your radar, including Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young and the New Orleans Saints Tyler Shough.

Young has come out hot to start the 2026 season, with three touchdown passes in each of his first two games (and a rushing touchdown in Week 1). He took a nice step forward in his third season last year and appears to be hitting another level yet again.

The talent is there—he was a top overall pick in 2023 for a reason. But now the fantasy results are starting to follow after three seasons of being an afterthought.

Whether this is sustainable remains to be seen, but if you are scouring waivers for help at quarterback you can only afford to be so choosy. Young should be a top consideration.

Shough has now exceeded 22 fantasy points in each of his first two games, leading the Saints to a win and a tight overtime loss. The Saints appear to have some real juice in the passing game, even if his fantasy totals on Sunday were propped up somewhat by a quarterback-sneak touchdown.

But 662 passing yards and five total touchdowns through two games is a good sign. If Shough is available in your league he's a fantastic pickup.

We're digging pretty deep here, given that 12 of Cam Ward's 20 fantasy points on Sunday came from a pair of rushing touchdowns. But for deeper or superflex leagues, you may not have much of a choice but to take a chance on a fringe player, and Ward's rushing ability gives him just enough upside to consider.

Young and Shough are much better options. But if neither are available, you may have to roll the dice on Ward's legs and hope his arm takes a jump as the season progresses.

articles.title: Kyler Murray's Injury Status for Bucs Game Updated by Vikings HC After Win vs. Bears
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings improved to 2-0 after Sunday's 9-3 win over the Chicago Bears, and more good news could be on the way.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings improved to 2-0 after Sunday's 9-3 win over the Chicago Bears, and more good news could be on the way.

Per ESPN's Kevin Seifert , Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell announced after the game that quarterback Kyler Murray is expected to clear concussion protocol "pretty early in the week," giving him a strong chance to return in Week 3 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

"He's doing great," O'Connell said. "He's feeling well."

O'Connell didn't officially announce Murray as the starter for next week's game, but he showed good progress when he participated in all three practices last week on a limited basis.

Minnesota quarterback Carson Wentz, who replaced Murray when he suffered a concussion in Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers, threw for 143 yards in Sunday's win over the Bears. He made a few key throws in the fourth quarter to help the Vikings hold onto the lead.

Wentz has been solid in Murray's absence, but there's a chance that the two-time Pro Bowler could take Minnesota's offense to the next level. The Vikings will certainly be hoping that Murray completes his recovery in time to take on the Bucs next Sunday.

articles.title: Raiders Beat Chargers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Kirk Cousins, Herbert, Top Players
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are 2-0. Yes, this is real life.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are 2-0. Yes, this is real life.

Kirk Cousins and the Raiders upset the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, 26-14, marking the first time the team has opened the season with a pair of wins since 2021.

And they've done it without superstar tight end Brock Bowers. Here's a look at the top performers from the contest:

The result could have been far worse for the Chargers. The team fumbled a whopping six times during the game but somehow only lost one. It was a crucial one to lose, however, coming late in the fourth quarter to set up a massive touchdown for the Raiders.

The Chargers even gave away two points after a holding call in the end zone caused a safety, the fourth penalty against tackle Joe Alt. It was just one of those days for the Chargers.

While the Raiders are celebrating, the Chargers are now reeling after a very surprising 0-2 start to the 2026 season. It's the first time Jim Harbaugh has ever started a season winless after two games in his collegiate and professional coaching career.

There was plenty of excitement about this team coming into the season—especially on the offensive side of the ball, with Mike McDaniel hired to lead the offense—but Justin Herbert and the Chargers are floundering. Major questions will need to be answered in Los Angeles.

But in Vegas it's been a party. Tougher days are ahead, no doubt, but these Raiders have hit the ground running in the Klint Kubiak era.

articles.title: Cowboys Top Commanders Amid Daniels Injury, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Dak, Lamb, Pickens, More

articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys started the season with a demoralizing loss to the New York Giants, but they got back on track with a divisional win on Sunday.

The Cowboys, who were 4.5-point favorites over Washington (via FanDuel Sportsbook ), downed the Commanders 37-20 in their home opener.

The Cowboys came out hot, scoring on their opening drive after a touchdown pass from Dak Prescott to CeeDee Lamb. A field goal made it a 10-0 lead heading into the second quarter.

The Commanders got on the board in the second quarter, but another touchdown from Prescott made it a 17-3 lead. The Commanders answered on the following drive when Jayden Daniels found Stefon Diggs in the end zone.

Disaster struck for the Commanders at the end of the half when Daniels landed awkwardly on his left arm and exited with a gruesome injury. He was replaced by Marcus Mariota.

Dallas and Washington traded field goals to start the second half before Prescott found Ferguson in the end zone again to go up 27-13.

The Cowboys later extended it to a 17-point lead early in the fourth, but the Commanders stayed in it when Mariota threw a touchdown pass to Diggs.

Dallas put things away late in the fourth when Prescott notched his fourth touchdown pass of the game to make it a 37-20 lead.

Dallas looked more like the team it was expected to be coming into the season against the Commanders. The Cowboys' defense still has some work to do, but at least its offense was clicking in Week 2.

Washington is now 0-2, and it appears Daniels is set to miss some time, only making things more difficult for a team trying to get back to the playoffs.

articles.title: Updated 2027 NFL Draft Order After Week 2 Results, Who Could Texans & Jets Take?
articles.summary: The list of 0-2 teams in the NFL is quite surprising if you compare it to preseason expectations.
articles.body:
The list of 0-2 teams in the NFL is quite surprising if you compare it to preseason expectations.

The Houston Texans would have the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft if the season ended today.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are also inside the top five after Sunday's games.

Of course, the draft order will change over the course of the season, but it is surprising to see a few potential Super Bowl contenders in the mix with franchises we expected to struggle, like the Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins, at the top of the draft order.

2. New York Jets (via Indianapolis - 0-2)

9. Cleveland (via Los Angeles Rams - 0-1)

Jeremiah Smith is widely viewed as the best non-quarterback offensive prospect in the 2027 draft class.

The Ohio State wide receiver is already up to 400 receiving yards through three games this season. He also has three touchdown catches.

Houston and Tampa Bay don't have bad wide receiver rooms, but if they remain at the top of the draft order, they likely aren't going to go quarterback, like so many other franchises will.

Tampa Bay just lost a generational receiver in Mike Evans in the offseason. Smith could be a perfect fit alongside fellow Ohio Stater Emeka Egbuka in a revamped offense in 2027.

Houston needs more support behind Nico Collins, who has had his share of injury issues in the NFL.

Adding Smith to the C.J. Stroud-led offense would be a massive boost for the Texans.

Both the Texans and Bucs don't expect to be anywhere near the top of the draft order by season's end, but right now, looking at the film of a top prospect like Smith, can at least help ease the pain of an 0-2 start.

Trinidad Chambliss stood out the most among the class of 2027 quarterbacks during Week 3 of the college football season.

The Ole Miss quarterback led his team to a double-digit lead and then finished off the victory with a touchdown rush after LSU tied the contest in the fourth quarter.

Chambliss is one of the oldest top quarterback prospects in recent memory, but he's also more polished than most of the younger signal-callers.

The Atlanta Falcons and Miami Dolphins make the most sense for Chambliss of the 0-2 franchises in the NFL.

If Michael Penix Jr. or Tua Tagovailoa fails to work out in Atlanta in 2026, the Falcons might want to land Chambliss to take advantage of its core offensive players while it still can.

Miami makes a little less sense because it is in a longer rebuild and could be patient with a quarterback, but if it wants to try and win in 2027, Chambliss might be the best fit there as well.

Dante Moore was in desperate need of a bounce-back week.

The Oregon quarterback threw for 280 yards and four touchdowns in an 84-0 victory over Portland State.

The opponent won't matter much to NFL personnel, but the performance might since it helped reset Moore after a surprising Week 2 loss to Oklahoma State.

Moore is one of the younger prospects in the quarterback pool. He might be ideal for the Dolphins because of how many years their rebuild could take.

Other teams with quarterback needs will float up to the top of the draft order as the season goes on. Cleveland, the New York Jets and a handful of others could be after Moore as well.

Moore will have a chance to improve his draft stock in front of a national audience on Saturday, when Oregon opens up Big Ten play on the road against USC.

articles.title: Tom Brady adds $375M to his fortune with a FOX deal worth nearly $42M more than his NFL earnings
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady spent 23 seasons building a legendary NFL career, but his biggest financial milestone may have come after he left the field. The seven-time .
articles.body: Tom Brady spent 23 seasons building a legendary NFL career, but his biggest financial milestone may have come after he left the field. The seven-time Super Bowl champion is now earning a reported $375 million through his FOX Sports broadcasting deal, surpassing the $332.96 million he collected in NFL playing contracts. For Brady, retirement has opened a new chapter where his football knowledge is proving just as valuable as his playing ability.Tom Brady's FOX Sports contract eclipses his NFL playing salaryBrady's reported 10-year, $375 million FOX Sports agreement, signed in 2022, stands out even against the earnings of today's top NFL quarterbacks. The deal made him the network's lead NFL analyst, working alongside play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt.According to Spotrac figures cited by Sporting News, Brady earned around $332.96 million in NFL contracts during his career. His broadcasting deal is worth roughly $42 million more, despite covering a decade rather than 23 seasons.The comparison does not include endorsements, investments or other business ventures. Nor does the $375 million represent an upfront payment. Still, the figures highlight the scale of Brady's second career.His rise makes the contrast even more striking. The New England Patriots selected Brady with the 199th pick in the 2000 NFL Draft. He began as a sixth-round pick with a modest contract, but went on to win six Super Bowls with New England and another with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.Brady also earned three NFL MVP awards, 15 Pro Bowl selections and three first-team All-Pro honours. His highest reported playing earnings came in 2021, when he made about $39.4 million with Tampa Bay.By comparison, his FOX contract averages $37.5 million annually. That puts his broadcasting pay in a league of its own, especially when measured against his career earnings as a player.Tom Brady's broadcasting career turns football knowledge into fortuneBrady did not move straight from the field to the FOX booth. He took a year away after his final NFL season before making his broadcasting debut in 2024, calling the Dallas Cowboys' game against the Cleveland Browns with Burkhardt.The transition demanded a different skill set. As a quarterback, Brady could read a defence and react without explaining every thought. Television required him to put those instincts into words for millions of viewers.“To use your voice and vision for a live television audience, there’s a lot of adrenaline in that, but it was very different from when I played. I would probably see all these things, I didn’t have to verbalize them,” Brady said in reflecting on the transition.“I knew subconsciously what to do, and my body just took over because that’s how I trained it. When you embrace the uncertainty, you work as hard as you can to prepare yourself, knowing that you’re going to wish you had done some things over.”His contract also reflects the value networks place on live sports and recognisable talent. A familiar face with deep football knowledge can bring viewers to a broadcast, making top analysts a major investment for media companies.ESPN, for example, recently agreed to a six-year, $108 million extension with Joe Buck, reportedly worth about $18 million per year.Brady, meanwhile, is now in his third season as FOX's lead NFL analyst. His journey from a late draft pick to one of the game's most decorated players helped create the profile behind his broadcasting deal.His playing career built the name. articles.title: Week 3 Waiver Wire Breakout Fantasy Football Pickups from Sunday's Box Scores
articles.summary: Fantasy football seasons were potentially altered on Sunday with the injuries to Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels.
articles.body:
Fantasy football seasons were potentially altered on Sunday with the injuries to Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels.

There's no official word on either quarterback, but the injuries themselves didn't look good, as both players had to be carted to the locker room in some capacity.

The right waiver-wire pickup at quarterback is now vital for the fantasy football players who thought they would rely on Williams and Daniels to put up eye-popping numbers all season.

One of the potential waiver-wire adds is Daniels' backup, Marcus Mariota, who has served in this role plenty of times in his career.

There might also be a free-for-all on the waiver wire to land Bryce Young, who has put up some of the best numbers of any quarterback through two weeks.

There are breakout stars at other positions, too, but the biggest concern at the moment is which quarterbacks are available to land in place of Week 2's injured players.

The natural, and likely the most available, replacement in fantasy circles for Daniels is Mariota.

The veteran backup quarterback put up 111 yards and a touchdown with an 11-for-16 line in relief of Daniels on Sunday in Dallas.

Mariota threw for over 200 yards on six occasions last season for the Washington Commanders.

He's more than a serviceable player to slot in for Daniels, and in the long term, he might be the best option.

However, the short-term outlook isn't great with Washington taking on the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3.

If you can manage through Week 3 with another quarterback, Mariota could be a solid option for clashes with the Indianapolis Colts and New York Giants in Weeks 4 and 5.

Daniels' prognosis is not yet known, but given the severity of the injury itself, it doesn't look like it'll be a one-week absence. Mariota might not be the leading passer every week, but he's usually reliable for between 150 and 200 yards and a touchdown contribution or two.

Bryce Young has arguably been the biggest fantasy football surprise through two weeks.

Young followed up his opening-week 361-yard outing with 287 yards and three touchdowns against the Atlanta Falcons.

The Carolina Panthers quarterback started the season in a perfect rhythm and has to be considered one of the top replacements for Williams and/or Daniels, if available.

Young plays the Cleveland Browns and Detroit Lions in the next two weeks before an early Week 5 bye.

The matchups combined with the early-season production make him one of the must-have quarterbacks on the waiver wire, not just to replace injured players, but to take over for underperformers at the position.

Emanuel Wilson's Week 2 workload was one of the more stunning takeaways from Sunday.

Wilson carried the ball 21 times for 92 yards inside the Seattle Seahawks offense. He had just two carries for three yards in Week 1.

Wilson had eight more carries and 40 more yards than rookie Jadarian Price, who many people thought would take Kenneth Walker's starting spot with Walker now in Kansas City.

The Week 2 splits made it feel like more of an open competition than we first expected.

Of course, it's still an early sample size, but the fact that Seattle relied so much on Wilson on Sunday, at least makes him an intriguing pickup for a Week 3 matchup against Washington in which the Seahawks will be heavily favored and expected to run the ball a ton.

Tre Tucker exploded for 119 yards and a touchdown for the Las Vegas Raiders against what was supposed to be one of the better defenses in the Los Angeles Chargers.

Tucker averaged 23.8 yards per catch on Sunday for the 2-0 Raiders.

Tucker can be a little boom or bust because of his big-play potential, but it is notable that he led Raiders wide receivers in targets with seven and receptions with five.

With Brock Bowers still out, there's a huge gap in production that the Raiders need to make up for. Tucker slid into that role on Sunday.

A Week 3 clash with the New Orleans Saints should produce fruitful numbers again for Tucker. He's best as a FLEX or a bottom-tier WR2 in most lineups, but if he puts up similar numbers as he did on Sunday, he could be valuable piece to lineups, even when Bowers eventually returns.

articles.title: Alec Pierce Injured, Latest Updates on Colts WR's Heel After Being Carted Off vs. Chiefs
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are dealing with an injury to their star receiver.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are dealing with an injury to their star receiver.

Alec Pierce exited Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs in the first quarter because of a heel injury. He was carted to the locker room after spending time in the medical tent.

The Colts ruled Pierce out in the second quarter. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that X-rays came back negative, and Pierce will undergo further evaluation on Monday.

Pierce was running a route and appeared to get a bit tripped up before hobbling off the field. He had one reception for 11 yards before exiting.

While it appears to be a heel injury rather than an ankle injury, it's worth noting that Pierce underwent surgery on his ankle in March and started training camp on the physically unable to perform list, from which he was not activated until late August.

Pierce, a 2022 second-round pick, is coming off a career-best season in which he recorded 47 catches for 1,003 yards and six touchdowns, leading the Colts' receiver room.

In last week's 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens, Piece had a team-high four receptions for 61 yards.

While the severity of Piece's injury is to be determined, the Colts will need to find some offense elsewhere until he's back on the field. Josh Downs will presumably be Daniel Jones' top offensive option, and Keenan Allen will likely see an increase in targets.

Jones should also look to tight end Tyler Warren as an additional option.

Injuries to star players have unfortunately been the storyline for the Colts over the last year. Indianapolis was on its way to the playoffs last season when Jones suffered a season-ending torn Achilles, and the team went on to miss the postseason following an 8-2 start.

The Colts are hoping to get back to the playoffs for the first time since 2020 this year, but a lengthy injury to Pierce would make that goal very difficult.

articles.title: They entered the season as Super Bowl hopefuls. Now the odds are against them.
articles.summary: The Los Angeles and Houston Texans -- who entered as Super Bowl contenders -- will face an uphill climb to simply make the playoffs after starting the season 0-2.
articles.body: On paper, both the Los Angeles Chargers and Houston Texans entered the NFL season in enviable positions: They each have talented quarterbacks (the Chargers’ Justin Herbert, the Texans’ C.J. Stroud), head coaches with a track record of success (Jim Harbaugh and DeMeco Ryans), and started the season with two home games. After two weeks, however, both Los Angeles and Houston will face an uphill climb to simply make the playoffs, let alone make a postseason breakthrough. The Texans fell to 0-2 on Sunday after a 20-6 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, with the Chargers joining them after a 26-14 defeat at the hands of the Las Vegas Raiders. For Houston, Week 2 saw the script flip from its Week 1 loss against the Buffalo Bills. Against the Bills, the Texans’ defense crumbled against Josh Allen. Against the Bengals, Houston’s defense played relatively well against the high-powered trio of Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, sacking Burrow five times and holding Cincy to only 20 points. But this week, the offense was inefficient. Stroud completed only 30 of a whopping 55 passes for 353 yards. He was sacked four times and did not throw a touchdown pass. The ground game wasn’t much better, as the Texans’ running backs ran the ball 14 times for 18 yards. (Stroud and receiver Jaylin Noel combined for 42 yards on four other carries.) “The one key to this victory was controlling the front and from an offensive perspective we did not control their front,” Houston head coach Ryans said postgame. “We got outplayed up front. We couldn’t run the ball well and that forced us into a lot of passing situations.” The concern will now continue to surround Stroud. A week after he fumbled on a potential game-winning drive, the fourth-year quarterback couldn’t keep up with Burrow, who completed a higher rate of his passes with more yards per attempt. Speaking of disappointing quarterback play...the Chargers didn’t inspire much confidence in their second-straight loss. Los Angeles has now scored only 14 points in back-to-back weeks, and has dropped games against teams who owned the first (Raiders) and third (Arizona Cardinals) overall picks in the most recent NFL draft. Herbert is still looking for success under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. After throwing for 209 yards, one touchdown and one interception with a 63% completion percentage in Week 1, Herbert was worse in Week 2, finishing with only 192 yards passing, one touchdown, two interceptions and a 56% completion percentage against Las Vegas. Though he struggled, Herbert was far from the Chargers’ only problem. The offense was also plagued by drops, penalties, fumbles and poor offensive line play. “We’re losing in the margins, that’s what we have to get fixed,” Los Angeles coach Harbaugh said postgame, adding several times that his team will need to get “back to work.” “We just have to better, that’s not good enough,” Herbert said after the loss. When asked about the team’s sloppiness, Herbert said the mistakes can ultimately be corrected by better execution. Both the Chargers and the Texans now face long odds to make the playoffs. Since 2020, when the NFL postseason expanded to 14 teams, only 16% of teams that have started 0-2 have made the playoffs. And for good measure, in NFL history, only three teams have started 0-2 and won a Super Bowl. That was certainly a preseason goal for the Chargers and Houston, who have high expectations based on the quarterbacks alone. The Texans, at least, have some experience in this situation. Houston started last season 0-3 before making the playoffs. “Sadly, we’ve been here before, but I think we just have to hold each other accountable,” Stroud said postgame. “We have to get better. There are a lot of things that we need to be doing better if we’re going to win.” Harbaugh, meanwhile, is now 0-2 to start a season for the first time in his career. “I’m not deterred, no one in that locker room is deterred,” Harbaugh said. “I like the way we fought. And that’s what it’s going to take, we have to fight our way out of this.”

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Says He Has to Do 'Better Job' of Telling Steelers' Mike McCarthy What Isn't Working
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers told reporters following Sunday's 20-3 loss against the New England Patriots that he needs to do a better job communicating to head coach Mike McCarthy which plays and schemes aren't working.
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers told reporters following Sunday's 20-3 loss against the New England Patriots that he needs to do a better job communicating to head coach Mike McCarthy which plays and schemes aren't working.

"Can't feel sorry for ourselves. Can't point fingers. We've all got to play better," he noted. "I think we can all give a little more. The best teams are player-led teams. We've got to keep taking the ownership. In a game like today where there wasn't a lot of flow to it, we need to be better, and that starts with me at making sure Mike knows what's working, what's not working, our coaches know, so we can call stuff that we feel like has a better chance.

Rodgers did suggest that play-calling wasn't the team's issue on Sunday, though he seemed to hint that perhaps the game plan was a bit bloated.

"It's not that big of a sample size, but I thought we didn't execute very well at all," he told reporters. "The plays were fine. We had opportunities, and we've got to dig into the details on some of this stuff. If there's too much stuff in the plan, we've got to cut it back. I always like to push the envelope. If I see guys doing it the right way in practice, then I feel good about it, but we've got to practice the practice to the game, obviously, and all the details that come with it."

Rodgers was pretty pedestrian himself, finishing Sunday's loss 23-of-39 with no touchdowns, an interception and four sacks taken. He also fumbled twice and lost one and the Steelers managed just 235 yards of total offense and were a woeful 2-of-12 on third downs.

Rodgers was a bit better in Week 1 against the Atlanta Falcons, throwing for 221 yards and a touchdown without any turnovers during the 20-13 win. New England's defense provided a much stiffer challenge, however.

"Offensively, clearly not good enough," McCarthy said of the offense after two weeks. "That starts with me. Felt it in practice frankly, coming off of last week. As I stated, I felt we were real herky-jerky trying to get in the run and pass. The extra time that you put forth, what you're expecting in a game and you don't deliver, it just tells you you need to spend more time on it. What I'm referring to is we put a lot of time and energy into the protection component of how we felt today's game was going to go. Expected pressure, got pressure. As an offensive coach, I always welcome the opportunity to play against pressure defense. I think it's clearly an opportunity for big play potential. That was not the case today. We didn't answer the bell. Our protections weren't clean. We had opportunities, whether it was communication and breakdowns, clearly in the first half that took away some opportunities for big plays. The run game was a little bit herky-jerky."

Being without wideout Michael Pittman Jr. didn't help, though the Patriots generated enough pressure to keep Rodgers uncomfortable regardless.

Pittsburgh's offense wasn't great last year either, and the limitations of fielding a 42-year-old quarterback are impossible to ignore. The Patriots certainly exposed a number of the Steelers' offensive weaknesses on Sunday.

articles.title: What happened to Alec Pierce? Latest injury update after $116 million Indianapolis Colts WR is carted off during Week 2 clash against the Kansas City Chiefs

articles.body: Alec Pierce’s return from offseason ankle surgery took another turn Sunday, September 20. The Indianapolis Colts wide receiver left the Week 2 game against the Kansas City Chiefs after hurting his left heel. Pierce limped off the field, went into the blue medical tent and later left for the locker room on a cart.Alec Pierce suffers left heel injury while making a route cut against ChiefsAlec Pierce suffered a left heel injury during the first half of the Colts’ Week 2 game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, September 20. The wide receiver did not have the football when the injury happened. He was making a cut on his route when he appeared to hurt his lower left leg.Pierce had one catch before leaving the game. He limped off the field and went into the blue medical tent for evaluation before cameras later showed him being carted to the locker room. The Colts listed him as questionable to return with a heel injury, but he did not come back.The injury came after Pierce returned from offseason ankle and heel surgery. He missed much of training camp before returning to practice and playing in Indianapolis’ season opener against Baltimore on September 13. The Colts have not confirmed a connection between the surgery and his latest left heel injuryWhy Alec Pierce’s injury is especially concerning for ColtsPierce had only recently completed a long recovery. On March 27, he underwent a procedure on his ankle after dealing with an issue that had bothered him since the end of the 2024 season. A PRP injection after the 2025 season failed to solve the problem, which led Pierce and the Colts to choose surgery.The procedure kept him out of OTAs and minicamp and forced him to miss training camp. On August 27, Indianapolis removed Pierce from the physically unable to perform list and allowed him to begin practising again. The Colts said he would need a gradual ramp-up before returning to full football activity.Pierce then played in the September 13 season opener against the Baltimore Ravens, catching four passes for 61 yards on six targets. He finished that campaign with 47 catches for 1,003 yards and six touchdowns while leading the NFL with 21.3 yards per catch for the second straight season.Currently, the key update remains simple: Alec Pierce suffered a left heel injury against the Chiefs on September 20 and did not return. articles.title: Cowboys vs. Ravens NFL Brazil Game Will Be Held at Maracana Stadium Despite Complaints About Field
articles.summary: Recent complaints about the field at Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro have led to questions about whether the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens should play there in Week 3, but the NFL has no plans to change the venue.
articles.body:
Recent complaints about the field at Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro have led to questions about whether the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens should play there in Week 3, but the NFL has no plans to change the venue.

Per Front Office Sports' Mark Maske , the NFL plans to move forward with Maracanã Stadium and "has a plan in place to ensure a high-quality playing surface."

Questions arose about the field at Maracanã Stadium in recent days after soccer players voiced their concerns about it.

"You don't even need to talk about the field. It's there for everyone to see," Flamengo goalkeeper Agustín Rossi said, according to ge, a Brazilian sports media site (h/t Jonas Shaffer of the Baltimore Banner) . "The way we play, it's unbelievable that we're playing on a field like this. Both penalty areas are bad as [expletive]. If you look at it, there are bumps everywhere. There's still going to be an NFL game here during the international break. After that game, I hope the field is in better shape."

It's not unheard of for the NFL to move international games to the regular NFL venues on short notice.

In 2018, a game between the Kansas City Chiefs and Los Angeles Rams was moved from Mexico City to the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum because of the field conditions at Estadio Azteca. The change was made less than a week before the game.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said after Sunday's win over the Washington Commanders that the team has "no concerns" about the field conditions, while owner Jerry Jones said they will monitor the situation.

"We'll look at that and I know it's the utmost concern to the league and the teams playing down there," Jones said, per the Dallas Morning News . We'll obviously stay informed as we look to it and it's front of mind now that we've gotten past the Washington Commanders."

While bringing NFL games to international venues has been a priority of NFL commissioner Roger Goodell in recent years, the health and safety of players will surely be the biggest concern.

For now, though, it seems the game will continue as originally scheduled.

articles.title: How Jayden Daniels’ mom supported his football ambitions before the Commanders made him the star QB
articles.summary: NFL News: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was carted off the field Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys after dislocating his left elbow on the fi.
articles.body: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was carted off the field Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys after dislocating his left elbow on the final play of the first half, the same elbow he injured last November against Seattle. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn confirmed it was a left elbow dislocation with no fracture, with more imaging scheduled later this week. The timing is brutal. Daniels was in the middle of one of his sharper performances this season before the play fell apart. Now, as Washington falls to 0-2, attention turns back to the man behind the jersey and the woman who made sure he got there.How did Jayden Daniels' mom shape his path to the NFL?Jayden Daniels' parents, Regina Jackson and Javon Daniels, met while both were students at Cajon High School in California, the same school their son would later attend. Football was always part of the family DNA. Javon is a big reason Jayden got into the sport at all. "When he was born, when he was old enough to walk, you hand him a ball, and I said, 'this is what you're gonna do,'" Javon said at the Heisman Trophy ceremony.But it was Regina who kept the engine running. "My mother has never missed a game," Daniels said on "The Pivot" podcast. "If it's raining out there, she's going to be out there. If it's minus degrees, she's going to be out there standing up the whole time making sure she's cheering me on." That is not hyperbole. From Arizona State to LSU to the NFL Draft, Regina Jackson showed up. Every single time."The word perseverance is that kid Jayden," she said before the Heisman Trophy ceremony. "The patience he has, the resilience to continue day after day, hour after hour, minute after minute, to be the best version of himself — just watching him get up at 5:30 in the morning to be great is really hard to describe."Daniels has been equally open about how much she means to him off the field too. "Nothing gets past my mama," he said. "She reads people and doesn't put people around me that don't benefit me. My mom's support through this journey has been huge."Why did Jayden Daniels' mom become a certified NFL agent?Regina Jackson did not stop at being a fan in the stands. She became an NFLPA-certified agent after passing the exam administered in late July 2024, making her likely the first parent of a top-three draft pick in NFL history to earn that designation. She holds an MBA with a concentration in entrepreneurship and a master's degree in public service administration. This was not a vanity project."Role number one, she plays my mom. From there, she's my business manager, and then also she is a certified NFL agent," Daniels said. As of March 2026, she became his only listed agent after he parted ways with Agency 1 Sports Group. With a contract extension on the horizon, her role has never mattered more.When Daniels suffered a hamstring injury and fans started drawing comparisons to Robert Griffin III, Jackson quickly shut it down on social media: "I wish you would stop manifesting RGIII on my son. Words are powerful and that's all that's talked about." She protects the narrative as fiercely as she protects his circle.Now, as Daniels heads into another injury scare with Washington needing answers fast, his mother is again at the center of the storm. Not watching from a distance. Right there.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $90M fortune gets attention, but his nearly $2M commitment to Kansas City kids reveals the community impact behind his NFL success
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce’s estimated $90 million fortune tells one part of his story. His long-running connection with Kansas City children tells another. The Chi.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s estimated $90 million fortune tells one part of his story. His long-running connection with Kansas City children tells another. The Chiefs tight end has contributed nearly $2 million to Operation Breakthrough over the years through personal donations and directed funds, while his Eighty-Seven & Running Foundation has helped support programmes that give young people access to education, technology and career skills.That relationship is still active in 2026. On Aug. 15, children from Operation Breakthrough watched the Chiefs’ preseason opener from Kelce’s suite at Arrowhead Stadium. A month later, his father, Ed Kelce, visited the organisation, read to first graders and shared childhood photographs of Travis and Jason Kelce.How Travis Kelce’s Kansas City work goes beyond a charity donationThe nearly $2 million figure comes from the Kansas City Chiefs, who reported it on Jan. 7, 2026, after Travis Kelce won Nationwide’s 2025 Charity Challenge. The $35,000 prize from the challenge went to Operation Breakthrough, adding to the support Kelce had already provided to the Kansas City organisation over the years.His relationship with Operation Breakthrough began long before his current level of NFL fame. Through Eighty-Seven & Running, Kelce supported the organisation’s robotics programme. That connection later grew into support for the Ignition Lab, a workforce development programme designed for students between 14 and 18.Travis Kelce has spoken openly about why the project became important to him. In comments carried by the Los Angeles Times, he recalled visiting Operation Breakthrough early in his Chiefs career and asking where the children went after reaching high school. “And I was like, man, we’ve got to do something about that,” Kelce said.The Ignition Lab opened in fall 2021 inside a former muffler shop that was purchased for the project through Eighty-Seven & Running. Operation Breakthrough says around 400 students spend time there each week, learning through hands-on programmes that include graphic design, mechatronics, green technology, automotive engineering, culinary arts, digital media and product design.For teenagers, the facility offers something more practical than a one-day celebrity visit. They can work with equipment, develop technical abilities and explore careers while they are still in high school.Travis Kelce’s $90M fortune is only one part of his Kansas City storyCelebrity Net Worth currently estimates Travis Kelce’s fortune at $90 million. The site also lists his fully guaranteed Chiefs cash compensation for 2026 at $12 million, with incentives that could take the figure to roughly $15 million.Those figures show the financial scale of Kelce’s NFL career, but he has repeatedly pointed to the children rather than the recognition when discussing his community work.“I don't do it for the awards, I don't do it for the acknowledgment. I do it for the smiles on the kids' faces at the Ignition Lab and at Operation Breakthrough,” Kelce said in 2024, according to KMBC.That approach has remained visible in Kansas City. The latest family connection came on Sept. 17, when Ed Kelce visited Operation Breakthrough. He read to first graders and showed them photographs of Travis and Jason from their childhood. The organisation shared the visit on social media, while Jason Kelce later praised his father for taking part in the event.Travis Kelce launched Eighty-Seven & Running in 2015 with a focus on helping disadvantaged young people through areas including education, business, athletics, STEM and the arts. His support for Operation Breakthrough has become one of the clearest examples of that work in Kansas City.So while Travis Kelce’s estimated $90 million fortune remains a headline number, his nearly $2 million in support for Operation Breakthrough points to another part of his career. His foundation has helped put young people closer to technology, creative work and career opportunities, with the Ignition Lab continuing that work beyond the football field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce's latest NFL record says plenty about what made the Chiefs star so difficult to bring down after catches
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce added another unusual entry to his NFL résumé on Sunday, moving past Marshall Faulk to become the league’s all-time leader in career yard.
articles.body: Travis Kelce added another unusual entry to his NFL résumé on Sunday, moving past Marshall Faulk to become the league’s all-time leader in career yards after the catch. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end reached the mark during the team’s matchup with the Indianapolis Colts, giving fresh weight to one of the most recognizable parts of his game. Kelce has never needed to rely only on speed to create extra yards. His balance, strength and feel for space have repeatedly allowed him to turn ordinary completions into bigger gains. That skill now has a record attached to it.How did Travis Kelce become the NFL’s all-time YAC leader?The record is a useful way to understand why Kelce has been such a difficult matchup for defenders. Yards after the catch measure what happens once a receiver secures the ball, and Kelce has spent much of his career making that part of the play count.In 2024, the Chiefs noted that Kelce had already moved into fourth place all time in career yards after the catch, with 5,632 yards at that point. Marshall Faulk led the list with 6,230. Kelce’s ability to close that gap is striking because Faulk was a running back known for his receiving work, not a tight end operating in the middle of an NFL passing game.Kelce has often made the first defender miss or simply powered through contact. He can catch a short pass, turn upfield and keep moving instead of settling for the yardage created by the throw. That has been a major part of his value to Patrick Mahomes and Kansas City over the years.The milestone also adds another layer to a career already filled with receiving records. Kelce has consistently produced from different areas of the field, whether lined up tight to the formation, in the slot or outside.What made Travis Kelce’s latest milestone stand out?The timing gave the record an extra bit of attention. Kelce also scored his first touchdown of the 2026 season against Indianapolis, giving the Chiefs star a productive night beyond the statistical milestone. Sports Illustrated reported that Taylor Swift celebrated from a suite, pointing to her wedding ring and shouting, “That’s my husband!”The moment quickly spread online, but Kelce’s record is the more lasting part of the night. It reflects a skill that can be easy to overlook because it happens after the catch rather than at the point of it.There is also something revealing about the name Kelce passed. Faulk was one of the NFL’s most versatile offensive players, so taking the top spot from him highlights how unusual Kelce’s career has been. A tight end leading the league in a category heavily shaped by running backs and receivers is not a routine achievement.For Kansas City, it is another statistical marker tied directly to what Kelce has done best. He catches the ball, stays on his feet and keeps the play alive. Now, that part of his game sits alone at the top of the NFL record book.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How Patrick Mahomes' kids' names - Sterling, Bronze, and Golden tell a hidden story about his career
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes and his wife Brittany are parents to three kids -- Sterling Skye, Patrick \"Bronze\" Lavon Mahomes III, and Golden Raye, who arrived in .
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and his wife Brittany are parents to three kids -- Sterling Skye, Patrick "Bronze" Lavon Mahomes III, and Golden Raye, who arrived in January 2025. To most people, these are just unique names. But look a little closer and a pattern appears -- one that connects directly to the metals that define athletic achievement, and quietly mirrors the arc of one of the NFL's most decorated careers.Why did Patrick and Brittany Mahomes choose metal-themed names for their kids?The metallic naming tradition in the Mahomes household did not begin with children. It started with dogs. While still in college, Patrick gifted Brittany a pit bull named Steel -- a nod to the Pittsburgh Steelers. They later added another dog named Silver. By the time their first child came along, the theme had already taken root.Sterling Skye arrived in February 2021, just as Mahomes was cementing himself as one of the most dangerous quarterbacks in the league. Sterling — a reference to sterling silver -- carries a meaning that goes beyond decoration. The word itself signals genuine quality. Something that holds its value. For a quarterback who had already won a Super Bowl MVP before turning 25, the timing felt fitting, even if unintentional.Bronze followed in November 2022, and the story behind that name is more personal. Mahomes has said they were originally going to name their son Trey, since he was Patrick Lavon Mahomes III. It was his brother Jackson who pushed for something different. "He can have his own thing now, where he's not Patrick, he's Bronze," Mahomes explained. The nickname stuck, and with it came an identity separate from the weight of a famous last name.Then came Golden Raye in January 2025 -- the newest member of a family that now numbers five. Gold, in any context, sits at the top. It is the standard everything else gets measured against.Do Patrick Mahomes' kids' names reflect his Super Bowl legacy?The connection is hard to ignore. Sterling, Bronze, Golden -- the three metals of the Olympic podium, and the three children of an athlete who has built one of sport's most dominant dynasties. Whether Mahomes intended it that way is another matter, but the symbolism lands.Laurie Kramer, a professor of applied psychology at Northeastern University, noted that names like these carry dual purpose. "The intention was to build unity in the family," she said. "Everybody's got a metal name in some way, so these kids would feel connected, and it was helping build a family identity around metals which could convey strength and resilience." But Kramer also flagged something worth thinking about: metals come with a built-in ranking. Gold outranks silver. Silver outranks bronze. "When you get names that come with a built-in hierarchy like gold, silver, and bronze, there may be some unintended side effects," she said.Brittany Mahomes has spoken openly about how each name felt right at the time. Sterling was set before they even knew the baby's gender. Bronze evolved naturally once the decision was made to keep the Mahomes name going into a third generation. Golden completed the trio.Together, the three names do something accidental but compelling -- they trace a quiet narrative of a career still being written. Sterling for the early proof of brilliance. Bronze for the continuity of legacy. And Golden, the latest and perhaps most loaded, arriving just as the question of where Mahomes lands all time is being asked more seriously than ever.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2012, NFL legend Joe Thomas bought a 1,200-acre Wisconsin farm with five cows and a bull; 14 years later, Hall of Fame Farms spans 4,100 acres and raises hundreds of cattle, including Wagyu
articles.summary: NFL News: Former Cleveland Browns star Joe Thomas has taken an unexpected turn after retiring from football, trading the NFL field for life on a Wisconsin farm..
articles.body: Former Cleveland Browns star Joe Thomas has taken an unexpected turn after retiring from football, trading the NFL field for life on a Wisconsin farm. The Pro Football Hall of Famer is the owner of Hall of Fame Farms, a cattle operation located in the state’s Driftless Region. Thomas spent 11 seasons with the Browns before retiring in 2018 and was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2023. According to Fox News, his interest in farming grew while he was still playing, eventually leading him to build a substantial agricultural operation with his family. Farm Progress has also reported on Thomas’ work on the farm and his approach to raising cattle.From football to farmingThomas, who grew up in Wisconsin, has spoken about wanting to own land long before his NFL career ended. He purchased the original property in 2012, while still playing for Cleveland, and initially started with just a handful of cattle.What began as a family farm eventually developed into a much larger agricultural operation. Fox News reported in September 2026 that the property has grown from the original 1,200 acres to roughly 4,100 acres and now includes hundreds of cattle, with Wagyu increasingly becoming a focus of the business. The transition also reflects a broader change in Thomas’ life after football. Following his retirement, he became increasingly interested in food, nutrition and the way cattle are raised. Farm Progress reported earlier this year that Thomas and his farm team emphasize nutrition and individual attention when caring for the herd.A different kind of Hall of Fame careerThomas’ football résumé gives the farm its distinctive name. Selected third overall by the Cleveland Browns in the 2007 NFL Draft, he played his entire 11-season career in Cleveland. The numbers remain remarkable. Thomas made 10 consecutive Pro Bowls, earned six first-team All-Pro selections and played 10,363 consecutive offensive snaps. The Pro Football Hall of Fame lists him as a member of its Class of 2023.That reputation for consistency has now become part of the identity of his agricultural business. Hall of Fame Farms presents the operation as a long-term family project rather than simply a celebrity venture, with Thomas and his wife, Annie, raising their children around the farm.What happens on the farmThe cattle operation focuses on both Wagyu and Certified Angus beef. According to Hall of Fame Farms, its cattle are pasture-raised before being corn-finished, while the farm uses selected genetics and a nutrition programme developed with a cattle nutritionist. The company also says it works with Full Blood Wagyu genetics.The farm’s approach is built around low-stress handling and close attention to animal care. Farm Progress similarly reported that Thomas’ team places considerable emphasis on nutrition and individual care for the cattle. The business now sells a range of beef products, including Wagyu steaks, Certified Angus beef, smoked meats and beef tallow. Its online operation allows customers to order cuts directly from the brand.Building something beyond footballFor Thomas, farming represents a second chapter rather than a complete break from his sporting career. articles.title: Chiefs Beat Colts in OT, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Mahomes, Kelce, Daniel Jones, JT, More
articles.summary: Overtime in Kansas City. Sunday Night Football had a thriller on its hands.
articles.body:
Overtime in Kansas City. Sunday Night Football had a thriller on its hands.

Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs closed out the weekend with an exciting 33-30 overtime victory over Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts.

The Chiefs, led by their two-time NFL MVP quarterback, entered Sunday night's matchup as a 6.5-point favorite over the Colts at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, per Fanduel Sportsbook .

A near game-sealing fumble by the Indianapolis Colts in overtime briefly had fans celebrating a premature victory, the Chiefs got it done their way, running down the clock and converting two field goals to seal the overtime win.

After missing the playoffs last season and losing Mahomes in Week 15 to a torn ACL and LCL, the Chiefs look like they are back to their Super Bowl-winning form, kicking off the 2026 season 2-0.

Jones and the Colts opened the contest with a 6:35 drive down the field, connecting with Tyler Warren for a short touchdown pass to take a 7-0 lead.

The rest of the first quarter was a nightmare for Indianapolis, allowing a Chiefs field goal before Jones threw an interception. Mahomes capitalized on the turnover with a quick touchdown connection to Travis Kelce to close out the first quarter with Kansas City leading 10-7.

Mahomes added a touchdown pass to Xavier Worthy, but a missed 51-yard field goal and a big quarter from the Colts helped Indianapolis overcome Kansas City's strong first quarter.

Indianapolis added two field goals in the second quarter before Jonathan Taylor ran in a 24-yard touchdown, giving the Colts a 20-17 lead at the break.

A nearly seven-minute drive out of halftime ended with Jalen Royals catching a touchdown pass for the Chiefs on a clutch fourth-down play, giving Kansas City a four-point lead heading into the final quarter.

After the Chiefs nailed a short 28-yard field goal to open the fourth, Taylor ran in his second touchdown of the night to tie things up at 27, where it would stay to send the game into overtime.

Kansas City got the ball first in overtime, setting up Harrison Butker for a 31-yard field goal to take a three-point lead.

Indianapolis' Laquon Treadwell pulled in a 48-yard pass from Jones on the Colts' opening drive of overtime that nearly was fumbled away for a Chiefs victory. After review, the call was overturned, determining he was down by contact and keeping the drive alive. Spencer Shrader then knocked down a field goal to tie it up once more.

Giving Mahomes the ball back with enough time to march down the field sealed the Colts' fate, with Butker nailing the game-winning field goal after a 46-yard drive.

Kansas City will face the 0-2 Miami Dolphins on the road next Sunday, while Indianapolis hosts the Houston Texans, also 0-2, the same day.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker shine as Chiefs beat Colts 33-30 in OT
articles.summary: Harrison Butker kicked two field goals in overtime, the second a 40-yarder that Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker III set up as time expired, giving the Kansas City Chiefs a 33-30 victory over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday night.
articles.body: Harrison Butker kicked two field goals in overtime, the second a 40-yarder that Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker III set up as time expired, giving the Kansas City Chiefs a 33-30 victory over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday night. Mahomes finished with 382 yards passing and three touchdowns, Walker ran for 117 yards, and Travis Kelce looked like a younger version of himself with nine catches for 101 yards and a score as the Chiefs improved to 2-0. Daniel Jones had 210 yards passing with a touchdown and a pick for the Colts. Jonathan Taylor had 92 yards rushing and two TDs. The Chiefs thought they had won the game earlier in overtime on a bizarre sequence of events. Butker kicked a 31-yard field goal to give them the lead, and the Colts (0-2) responded on their possession by having Jones throw deep to Laquon Treadwell, who had beaten L’Jarius Snead. Treadwell appeared to be bobbling the ball as he hit the ground, got up after he had completed the catch, had the ball popped loose and watched as the Chiefs pounced on it. The play was ruled a fumble on the field, but the officials reviewed it and determined Treadwell was down by contact. That gave the Colts a chance to score a go-ahead touchdown, but they ended up having to settle for Spencer Shrader’s tying 38-yard field goal. The Chiefs took over once more with 3:11 left in the extra session, and they handed off to Walker on three straight plays to reach midfield. But the backbreaker for Indianapolis was a 22-yard pass to the running back, which set up Butker’s winning kick.

Maddux Madsen was 22-of-31 passing for 208 yards with a pair of touchdown passes for Boise State (2-1). Sire Gaines added 102 yards rushing, including a short-yardage scoring run that tied the game 14-14 midway through the second quarter. Rasean Jones had a 9-yard touchdown catch and finished with eight receptions for 95 yards for the Broncos. Cam Bates also had a touchdown catch.

Modrzewski threw for 243 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions for South Dakota (3-1) of the Football Championship Subdivision, which is ranked 10th in the Stats Perform Top 25. articles.title: Brock Purdy Looks Unstoppable as 49ers Start 2-0
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are off to a 2-0 start, and Brock Purdy looks like a quarterback ready to take his game to another level. San Francisco dominated the...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers are off to a 2-0 start, and Brock Purdy looks like a quarterback ready to take his game to another level.

San Francisco dominated the Miami Dolphins 35-13 on Sunday, following up its Week 1 victory over the Los Angeles Rams with another convincing performance. The 49ers have now opened the season with consecutive wins of at least 20 points for the first time in franchise history.

The 26-year-old quarterback completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns without throwing an interception. He also rushed for 30 yards and a touchdown, finishing with a remarkable 149.1 passer rating. At one point, Purdy completed 18 straight passes.

What stands out most is how efficient Purdy has been.

The 49ers scored touchdowns on each of their first five drives, something they had not accomplished since 1991. Purdy consistently made the right reads, delivered accurate throws and kept San Francisco's offense moving despite Miami trying to slow down the run game.

He also showed his ability to make plays outside of structure. Purdy's connection with Mike Evans helped set up Christian McCaffrey 's second touchdown, while George Kittle added a 12-yard touchdown reception. Kyle Juszczyk also caught a touchdown pass from Purdy in the third quarter.

McCaffrey had another milestone performance, scoring twice to reach 100 career touchdowns in just 114 games, but Purdy's performance was the biggest reason San Francisco's offense looked so difficult to stop.

Through two games, Purdy has looked calm, aggressive and extremely efficient. Head coach Kyle Shanahan specifically praised his quarterback's growth and performance following Sunday's win.

There is still a long way to go in the season, but the early results are hard to ignore. The 49ers are 2-0, their offense is clicking and Purdy appears to be playing with tremendous confidence.

If he continues playing at this level, San Francisco could have something very special brewing.

articles.title: Cowboys beat Commanders, Vikings down Bears as star QBs injured
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys beat arch-rivals Washington 37-20 in a game marred by a gruesome injury to Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels, while the Chicago Bears...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys beat arch-rivals Washington 37-20 in a game marred by a gruesome injury to Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels , while the Chicago Bears lost their own signal-caller Caleb Williams in defeat to Minnesota on a brutal NFL Sunday.

Elsewhere Kansas City survived a late Indianapolis scare, but a number of favorites including the Baltimore Ravens fell to upset losses on week two of the 2026 season.

Dak Prescott threw for 279 yards and four touchdowns in Texas, surpassing former Dallas great Tony Romo for the most touchdown passes in Cowboys history, with 249.

"There's a lot of bigger numbers out there that I want -- a championship -- but we're just getting started," said Prescott, whose team improved to 1-1 after an opening-weekend loss to the Giants.

But his opposing quarterback Daniels bent his left elbow backward while tumbling from an accidental stamp by his own guard in the first half, and was carted off the field with a towel covering his head.

The 25-year-old re-injured the joint he dislocated last year, in another crushing blow to a Commanders franchise that the talismanic Daniels had carried to within a game of the Super Bowl in his thrilling rookie season.

"It was a dislocation. The X-ray showed no fracture," said Washington coach Dan Quinn.

"Man, are we bummed for him. I thought he was really playing his ass off."

After Daniels' departure Dallas stretched their 17-10 halftime lead, despite Washington backup QB Marcus Mariota finding Stefon Diggs for the receiver's second touchdown.

Earlier, Chicago's Williams pulled up in agony while scrambling in the red zone late in the Bears' rain-drenched loss 9-3 to the Vikings.

The disappointing home opener saw the Bears restricted to just a single field goal, one week after piling up 59 points against Carolina.

Williams was given no respite by the Vikings' steely defense all game, forced to scramble under repeated blitzes, suffering three sacks and coughing up an interception before his injury.

"A hamstring could be pretty damaging... We'll see how bad it is tomorrow," said Bears head coach Ben Johnson.

Patrick Mahomes ' Kansas City beat the Colts in the final second of overtime.

Kansas City had settled for a field goal on their first overtime possession. Colts receiver Laquon Treadwell appeared to fumble after catching a 50-yard pass, prompting wild Chiefs celebrations.

But after lengthy review, he was ruled to have already been brought down by marginal contact before the fumble, and Indianapolis tied it with a field goal.

The reprieve was not enough. Kenneth Walker III rushed the Chiefs into field goal territory again, and Harrison Butker sealed victory 33-30.

"We had a lot of errors, but I thought the guys were resilient," said Mahomes.

Among several upsets, the New Orleans Saints scored 15 unanswered fourth-quarter points for a shock 24-17 defeat of the Baltimore Ravens.

The comeback came a week after the Saints forced overtime from 21-0 down to Detroit but lost.

"Sometimes you have to learn how to win, learn how to finish... We're right on time," said Saints defensive edge Chase Young .

The Los Angeles Chargers suffered a second straight ignominious loss, falling 26-14 to unfancied AFC West rivals Las Vegas .

Cleveland 's under-pressure quarterback DeShaun Watson fired the Browns to a surprise 23-19 win in Tampa Bay, while Cincinnati receiver Ja'Marr Chase scored two touchdowns in a 20-6 Bengals win against Houston 's highly rated defense.

Reigning champions Seattle shrugged off their quarterback Sam Darnold 's injury absence, going 2-0 under backup Drew Lock with a 31-7 rout of Arizona .

The Philadelphia Eagles snatched a 24-20 win over Tennessee thanks to a last-gasp Darius Cooper touchdown, while New England bounced back with a clinical 20-3 defeat of Pittsburgh .

There were further injury woes in New York, as the Green Bay Packers grabbed a tense 20-17 overtime win.

Packers receiver Jayden Reed collided with a defender's shoulder pads and collapsed.

Reed has feeling and movement in all his extremities but will stay in hospital overnight, the team said.

"Doing much better," Reed posted on social media.

Mike Tomlin provided an insightful critique on Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers' offense following their 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots on Sunday afternoon.

Rodgers started the final year of his legendary NFL career, hoping for one last playoff run before hanging up the jersey for good. However, that objective will be difficult if the offense goes through inconsistent performances.

Rodgers completed 23 out of 39 passes for 187 yards and an interception, absorbing four sacks from the New England defense. He regressed from the opening win over the Atlanta Falcons , a sign that Pittsburgh's attack will have issues early on.

Tomlin, who was the longtime Steelers coach until he retired after the 2025 season, reflected on the team's performance. He pointed out a lack of identity as they navigate a new period with Mike McCarthy as the head coach while Rodgers plays his final NFL season.

"From my perspective, they don't have a place to hang their hat. They haven't established the run. They're not performing well enough on third down, or possession-down circumstances. And to make matters worse, they're not getting yards in chunks. They can't solve all their problems, but they better solve at least one of these problems, and really soon," Tomlin said, via Blitzburgh.

How Aaron Rodgers , Steelers played against Patriots

Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers have the talent to be in the mix for the playoff picture. However, their road loss to the Patriots show they have limits to their reach as a playoff contender.

Pittsburgh failed to record a touchdown throughout the game, only managing a field goal in the second quarter. Meanwhile, New England scored in all four quarters, an aspect that the Steelers need to improve moving forward.

articles.title: Raiders’ Bold Play-Calling Unleashes Kirk Cousins vs. Chargers
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins, who has been the subject of thinkpieces about his arm strength all week, quieted some critics. The quarterback fo...
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins , who has been the subject of thinkpieces about his arm strength all week, quieted some critics. The quarterback followed his coach's lead, rather than playing it safe against a rather porous Los Angeles Chargers defense.

Klint Kubiak could have played things very differently, settling for checkdowns and moving the ball downfield incrementally. Yet, in the aggressive play-calling, especially in the fourth quarter, the Raiders kept the action going. As a result, the hargers could not gain their footing and struggled to keep up. Cousins was honest when asked about the style change.

"I don't make those decisions. I have to be ready for the moment whenever that time calls for it. We did stay aggressive."

The Riders' starting quarterback and his head coach share a lengthy histor y. When Cousins excelled in Minnesota , Kubaika served as his offensive coordinator. Kubiak remains a devotee of the West Coast offense, with the zone bootleg system.

He wants Cousins to shift the pocket a bit, catching the defense in a metaphorical no man's land. Under those circumstances, utilizing play-action to reach the bootleg remains a major focus for the Raiders in the first two games. Furthermore, mixing in crossing routes downfield helps alleviate concerns about Cousins' perceived lack of arm strength.

The playful action, a staple all day, showed itself in the second half. The Raiders surprised the Chargers while holding a 17–14 lead with three minutes left in the second half, putting them well within field goal range. Cousins induced the defense to bite on a ball fake, which lured the safety downhill. Cody White slid free into the end zone on a third-and-five. In effect, if the Raiders kick a field goal there, the Chargers could still win with a touchdown. Kubiak had faith in Cousins to execute an almost flawless ball fake and identify White wide-open to secure the victory.

Now, no one will ever confuse Cousins' arm strength with Justin Herbert . However, throwing a quality deep ball is more than step and fire. Kubiak's scheme took advantage of Los Angeles 's lack of quality secondary play. In the first quarter, inside the Chargers' 50-yard line, Tre Tucker sprang loose, and Cousins connected on a 42-yard touchdown pass. The ball looked to have traveled 45 yards in the air. Nothing eye-popping, but the awareness of knowing your quarterback's strengths and weaknesses without ceding any of the three levels to the defense worked.

The Raiders ran 60 plays, with 29 coming through the air. The Chargers were pressuring Cousins' earl, hitting him from all angles. However, Kubiak helped slow their rush down with the short game. Getting the ball out fast negated the Los Angeles rush.

Furthermore, that extra bit of time helped Coisuins connect with eight different receivers. The lack of a conventional No. 1 wideout was another factor contributing to their success. Instead, Kubiak built the game plan around not just taking what's there, but making the Chargers pay for letting their eyes be tricked by play action.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes pre-game drink mystery solved after fans thought he drank alcohol before Chiefs-Colts
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes was caught on camera taking a huge swig from a bottle before their Week 2 game against the Indianapolis Colts. Mahomes...
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes was caught on camera taking a huge swig from a bottle before their Week 2 game against the Indianapolis Colts .

Mahomes is getting ready to show the NFL he can dominate as QB once again after requiring a nine-month absence to heal from his torn ACL.

It seems Mahomes will get ready for games by any means necessary, as fans started theorising about the QB potentially drinking vodka or limoncello before their clash against the Colts.

Patrick Mahomes was drinking pickle juice and not alcohol before the Chiefs game

Despite the video making fans spread the rumours that Mahomes was drinking vodka or limoncello when caught on camera taking a swig from a small bottle, the truth has been known for years.

The aforementioned post on X received over 1.5 million views in under four hours, with many other fans perpetuating this false notion as a result.

The Chiefs encourage their players to drink pickle juice before games to avoid cramping during games. While many debate whether this is effective, it's clear that NFL teams would rather indulge this practice than ignore it and miss out on any potential benefits.

It's erroneous and ridiculous to expect a multi-time MVP and champion like Mahomes to do shots of alcohol before an NFL game, so it's best to put the vodka theories to an end.

Patrick Mahomes has been drinking pickle juice before games for years

Mahomes has been drinking pickle juice before games for years, with the QB himself revealing in 2020 that this practice predates his time with the Chiefs.

"I've drank it since high school, actually, so it's like a little shot. Just got to knock it to the head and not try to taste it as much as possible."

"Well, the pickle juice usually is before, like you try to keep you from cramping. I don't know … might have to do with the sodium, I think. They try to keep you from cramping."

Mahomes went 32/47 on passing attempts for 382 passing yards, three touchdowns, and a 114.0 passer rating against the Colts, as the Chiefs won 33-30 in OT.

articles.title: Vikings Have Chance to Trade JJ McCarthy After Gruesome Injury in NFC East
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings now have a couple of potential options to try and trade quarterback JJ McCarthy ahead of the NFL's deadline. The post Vikings Have Chan...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings have already proven through two weeks that they do not need JJ McCarthy to win games, and with Kyler Murray probably on his way back to the starting lineup in Week 3, it is now time for the team to consider moving its former No. 10 pick.

More than one franchise could use McCarthy heading into Week 3, though the most desperate situation might involve the Washington Commanders . Quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow in gruesome fashion on Sunday, September 20 in a loss to the Dallas Cowboys that dropped his team to 0-2 on the season.

Daniels dislocated the same elbow in 2025 and missed three games.

"Ruled OUT now. Scary looking injury. Re-injury is never good," former NFL team doctor David Chao wrote on X Sunday. "But season not over. Can return more quickly than people think with a brace."

However, Chao also mentioned that the Commanders might consider surgery to render Daniels less prone to a third elbow injury. And that could potentially result in an even longer absence.

"Jayden Daniels, left elbow dislocated again. Will be ruled out today. Will likely miss time," Chao said in a social media video . "Commanders could consider surgery so the ligament does not dislocate so easily."

Commanders Have Solid Backup QB in Marcus Mariota , but JJ McCarthy Can Offer Hope for Higher Ceiling

Marcus Mariota stepped into the QB1 role and played efficiently enough, completing 11-of-16 passes for 111 yards and one TD . He did not turn the football over.

Mariota has been the backup in Washington since 2024. He has appeared in 14 games, including eight starts in 2025. Mariota is 2-6 as the Commanders' starter with 2,059 yards, 14 TDs and seven INTs .

Washington knows it has a reasonable option in Mariota to start a handful of games in Daniels' stead, but the franchise is also aware that their playoff hopes are slim to none without Daniels under center.

A hypothetical move for McCarthy would be layered, with the incentives including a young, motivated player with a potentially higher ceiling than Mariota, a future backup/alternative to Daniels if his injury issues continue and a superior QB2 option behind Mariota as opposed to seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis .

Vikings Are Undefeated, Leading NFC North Division With Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz at QB

There are perhaps more teams in immediate need of a starting quarterback than the Commanders, namely the Atlanta Falcons , who played Cooper Rush and Jack Strand on Sunday during a 34-3 home defeat at the hands of the Carolina Panthers .

The larger point is that injuries around the NFL to prominent quarterbacks are beginning to create a market in which the Vikings may be able to move McCarthy for a decent draft pick.

McCarthy lost his starting job to Murray in August before the team's first preseason game. He then fell to QB3 behind Carson Wentz just ahead of the season-opener against the Green Bay Packers .

Minnesota is now 2-0 with wins over the Packers and Chicago Bears , both NFC North Division opponents, and has not yet played McCarthy on a single snap.
